Welcome to the Emir's Arena! Are you interested in 1v1 Tournaments? We organise ranked Tournaments here, or alternatively you can organise your own unranked Tournaments.
What's a 1v1 Tournament?

A group of fighters is divided into pairs of opponents, and they all fight their opponent. The winners of those fights proceed to the next round, where they're divided into pairs, and they each fight their new opponent.
The number of surviving fighters is halved each time, until eventually only one person is left standing. They're the winner of the Tournament.
Ranked or unranked? What does that mean?
Everyone has a rank. It's meant to indicate how good they are at fighting, compared to other people.
In ranked fights, the winners gain rank and the losers lose rank. The Arena staff will decide who'll be fighting in each ranked Tournament, and send the invitations.
But if you just want some casual fun, you can have an unranked Tournament, where no-one gains or loses rank. You can organise your own unranked Tournament, and decide for yourself who'll fight in it.
Only the ranked fights offer access to the other rewards of the Arena.
How do I get invited into a Tournament?
You'll need to sign up to a recruitment group...
You can carry on with your adventures while you're waiting for a Tournament to begin, since it may be a while before suitable fighters are available.
I want to organise my own Tournament.
Just use my Recruitment Board here to form your own recruitment group. Once you've got one, wait for other fighters to join it.

We was sailin' along happily, and I was partakin' of a little 'rum' in the crows nest.
Well, we hit either a really rough wave or some rocks.

Beginner clues are the lowest tier of clue scroll and as such only require a couple of steps to solve.

Slaying monsters for a chance at a clue being dropped. I hear goblins are sneaky, maybe they have some clue scrolls on them ripe for the taking.

Advanced clues have tiers between easy and master.

What's this PIN thing that people keep talking about?

The PIN - Personal Identification Number - can be set on your bank account to protect the items there in case someone finds out your account password. It consists of four numbers that you remember and tell
no one.
So if someone did manage to get your password they couldn't steal your items if they were in the bank.
How do I set my PIN?

You can set your PIN by talking to any banker, they will allow you to access your bank pin settings. Here you can choose to set your pin and recovery delay. Remember not to set it to anything personal such as
your real life bank PIN or birthday.

The recovery delay is to protect your banked items from account thieves. If someone stole your account and asked to have the PIN deleted, they would have to wait a few days before accessing your bank account to
steal your items. This will give you time to recover your account.
There will also be a delay in actually setting the PIN to be used, this is so that if your account is stolen and a PIN set, you can cancel it before it comes into use!
How do I remove my PIN?

Talking to any banker will enable you to access your PIN settings. There you can cancel or change your PIN, but you will need to wait for your recovery delay to expire to be able to access your bank. This
can be set in the settings page and will protect your items should your account be stolen.
What happens if I forget my PIN?

If you find yourself faced with the PIN keypad and you don't know the PIN, just look on the right-hand side for a button marked 'I don't know it'. Click this button. Your PIN will be deleted (after a delay of a
few days) and you'll be able to use your bank as before. You may still use the bank deposit box without your PIN.

Should you choose to form your own clan you will need four friends to join you, and it is recommended that you have spent a good amount of time in this world first. Leadership is not for everyone.

Clans offer you the ability to have an official gathering of friends or like-minded individuals in a hierarchical structure.
In other words, you and your friends get an exclusive chat channel and a Clan Hall, as well as the ability to assign ranks to members.
Ranks can be assigned from custom pre-sets, which then determine what permissions that person has.
For example: One person may have the rank to kick players from the chat, while another has the rank to access the Clan Coffer.
What is the Clan Coffer?
The Clan Coffer is a shared coin store, used by members of the clan. Highly ranked members can assign who has permission to deposit and withdraw coins.
What is a Clan Hall?

A Clan Hall is a private area only accessible for the people with the permission to enter. High ranked members of the clan can restrict it to only allow certain ranks in, or open it up to even allow guests.

King Shayzien VII may have found a way to combine these powers.
How did Xeric have so much power?
Xeric drew much of his power from the Dark Altar, but he asserted his authority as ruler through his personal army of creatures, the lizardmen.
Xeric created the lizardmen!?

We have little written record of the experiments, but we believe they might have led to the creation of the lizardmen.
Do you know why he created the lizardmen?

Xeric was undoubtedly powerful, but he couldn't rule the people singlehandedly, nor could he rely on human informants. He needed an army he could control.
Lizardmen are loyal creatures and would do as he commanded without question. With them at his disposal, the people were powerless to resist his authority.

Blinded by fury, Byrne attacked the guard, slaughtering the lizardman in plain sight of all around.
Legend has it Byrne then gave a galvanizing speech, standing over the butchered guard with his bloodied pitchfork held aloft in the air, urging the people to fight back.

What is a Group Iron Man?
Group Iron Man is a game mode where you do everything as a group. You can only trade items with player's in your group, take their items and accept their help.

What is Individual Prestige?
Individual Prestige is automatically awarded to you the very first time you create a group. It is proof that you were one of the original members of that group.
This proof is displayed as a gold star next to your name on the group sidepanel. Note that if you join an existing group, you will not be considered an original member.
The limits are gold and items worth up to 1,000,000 coins for the 1st week, 20,000,000 coins for the 2nd week, 50,000,000 coins for the 3rd week and 100,000,000 coins for the 4th week.
During these 5 weeks you will also have restrictions to what you can equip: certain items will require you to have killed the monster that drops them.
What is Group Prestige?
Non-Hardcore groups can show their dedication to the group through Group Prestige. This status can be viewed on the group's sidepanel, just below the group's name.
Group Prestige is lost upon inviting new members into the group, or upon doing certain activities with players outside of your group.
What is a Hardcore Group Iron Man?
Hardcore Group Iron mode is a more challenging version of the regular mode, in which you have only a set number of lives for the entire group.
If you die in an unsafe area, you will lose one of your group's lives. When your shared lives hit 0, you will all be downgraded to regular Group Iron players.

But Zulrah, in his mercy, allowed some of those transgressors to live, sparing them the punishment they deserved, and allowing them the chance to repent.
Then my mother, oldest and wisest of the tribe, dared to intercede with the mighty Zulrah on behalf of her people, and thus a sacred contract was declared.
Zulrah granted us the right to dwell in his lands, and to eat of their bounty. None shall ever drive us out, for Zulrah protects us.
All he asks in return is a periodic sacrifice at his sacred shrine. As long as the sacrifices continue, Zulrah will let us live peacefully in his lands.

grew larger, it was hard to find enough food for everyone, and we were forced to shift our camp more and more often. In time, a warrior called Gunnar took his friends and their families and left the larger tribe,
moving south in search of new places. They eventually settled here and built this village, finding that the old nomadic traditions were no longer needed.
Our current chieftain, Gunthor the Brave, is a direct- line descendent of Gunnar.

However, our ways have changed little in the last century. Although more and more people use magical powers, we do not believe it is wise to take upon oneself the power of the gods in this way. To this day, we fight

with the mighty sword, the vicious axe and the swift arrow on the wind. Some of our young, wishing to try so-called 'civilisation' and the softness of city life, abandon the tribe and move to the cities. It is sad to
see them go, but we do not prevent them; we live here in our village because we love this life - we do not force it on those whom it does not suit.
There, I have said enough.
Thank you.
You look like a load of primitive savages.
And you look like an arrogant fool. And you smell like a raccoon's bottom.
I'm bored.
I came to kill you all!
Ho ho! Brave words indeed from an outerlander! Go down to the longhall and try it!
Well done.
You've [found a new clue/obtained a casket]!
Nothing much.
I'm exploring.

You look like a load of primitive savages.
I'm bored.
I came to kill you all!
Whoah there, stranger, careful where you're walking. I almost clobbered you there; thought you were a larupia or something.
What are you doing here?
Me? Oh, I'm just having some fun, capturing wild animals, living on the edge, stuff like that.
Hey, want me to teach you how to catch the critters around here? Ain't come across anything yet that I couldn't capture.
Ok, where's a good place to start?

Your easiest bet around here is probably to go for some of the birds. Go for the crimson swifts; they're the bright red ones that hang around near the coast. They're as obliging as can be, or maybe they're just
plain dumb, but either way they just seem to throw themselves into traps half the time.
What sort of traps should I use?
Just use a standard bird snare and you'll be fine. You can get them in any decent shop that sells Hunter gear.
How do they work, then?

Well, they're kind of sneaky, really. You've got a tall post with what appears to be a little perch sticking out the side. Now, the bird will see this as somewhere to sit, but the perch is actually rigged such that when the bird
lands on it, it'll drop away.
Further, as the perch drops, it releases a noose that tightens around the bird's feet and captures it. Neat huh?
So, was there anything else you wanted to ask about?
Thanks for your help.
Not a problem, any time.
What sort of things are there to catch around here?
What're you interested in? You've got anything from birds for beginners up to larupias for the pros, not to mention weasels, butterflies, barb-tails and chinchompas.
How would I go about catching birds?
There are a couple of varieties that you can try your hand at catching around here, but the technique for both is essentially the same. You need to set up a bird snare.
Further, as the perch drops, it releases a noose that tightens around the bird's feet and captures it. Neat, huh?
How do I get hold of a weasel?

Not with large quantities of rice and treacle as many people would have you believe. Besides, the Feldip weasel isn't technically a weasel, but, as is typical with any sort of colloquial name, it's been called that often enough
now that it's stuck.
Anyway, the Feldip weasel's main survival technique is in hiding; other than that, it's pretty stupid. So, if you can actually find one, then you've probably got a fairly good chance of catching one.
And how would I actually go about finding one?
The best place to start would probably be just south of here. You'll find lots of kebbit burrows there. Take a close look at some of them, follow the trails and you can't go far wrong.
Well, seeing as you seem to like larupias so much...
Ah yes, yes, larupias are fun; just think of them as big kittens.
Uh huh, big kittens that just want to rip your throat out!
Indeed, and you can use this to your advantage. If a larupia is keen to chase you then let it; that way you can happily lead it straight into your trap without any fuss or waiting around.
Into what sort of trap should I lead it?
A pit trap should do you. There are some appropriate pits to the east of here that you can use. Cover one with a few logs and branches, tease the kitty and then lead it to the pit. Simple.
Barb-tails sound interesting.

They do sound interesting, don't they? Unfortunately, they're actually just another type of kebbit; those things get everywhere. Still, the tails of these particular kebbits can be useful for fishing.
So, how would I go about catching one them?
Just squash them with a boulder, quick and simple.
What, you mean just pick up some boulders and start throwing them at kebbits? That doesn't sound simple.
No silly, you let the creature squash itself. Just use some sticks to hold a boulder in a nice precarious position, place some bait underneath and let the creature knock itself out.
What on earth is a chinchompa?
Awwww, chinchompas are great. They're highly volatile little balls of fluff. Cute as you like, but for some reason they do have this tendency to spontaneously combust.
What? Why?
Probably something to do with the fact they'll eat anything and everything, especially spicy food.
Anyways, if you want to capture a chinchompa, I suggest using a box trap. That way, if the little fluffball does explode, then at least most of the blast will be contained within the box.
Somehow butterflies don't strike me as your sort of thing.
Not really, but some people like them. The ones around here are at least vaguely interesting, though. The black ones are supposedly magical butterflies.
Doesn't that make them harder to catch?
Not particularly; you can still catch them using an ordinary butterfly net. Oh, and you'll probably need some butterfly jars in which to keep them as well.
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
There are four key factors that will affect your chances: what bait you use, how close to the trap you are, your appearance and your smell.
How does bait help?

Unfortunately, creatures don't just jump into traps for the fun of it nearly as often as we as Hunters might like. However, it is possible to improve those odds. If you can find the right bait to use on your trap,
something your prey really craves, then hunger overrides fear and the creature is just that little bit more likely to bounce to its furry little doom.
Why is it important how close I am to the trap?

However well you might be blending in, if you're standing with your nose pressed right up against your own trap, the poor little critters ain't going to go anywhere near it. So, you need to make sure you put
a sensible distance - I'd say at least four strides - between yourself and your trap.
Why would the creatures care about my appearance?

You're a human. From the point of view of a lot of creatures, you're big and scary. So, it'd be best if the furry little monsters didn't notice you. You need to blend in like the creatures themselves.
And how do I do that?

Easy, dress up like one of them. Even easier, dress up using the furs of the creatures themselves; then you're bound to get the colour right. And, I suppose, if you don't fancy just slinging a dead fur over your
shoulders, you can probably get them made into something more appealing. I hear there are tailors in Varrock who are good at that sort of thing.
What's wrong with my smell!?

I'm sure there's nothing wrong with your smell...from a human point of view. But to your prey, any trap that you've set up will reek of human, and that's going to work against you if you don't do anything about it.
So what should I do?

You need to mask that lovely human scent of yours with something else. Smoke works well. Take a lit torch and waft it around the trap a bit. You'll quickly overpower most of the other smells around the trap.
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
Well, the equipment isn't too hard to get hold of. You've got specialist shops like Aleck's in Yanille that'll see you right. He's a bit pricey, mind, but it's pretty decent kit.
The clothing is a tad trickier to get hold of, the materials required being rather difficult to seperate from their reluctant owners.
But, if you can get the furs, there are shops like the tailor's in east Varrock that can help you.
I think I'll give it a miss right now, thanks.
Suit yourself!

What's a larupia? You don't know? You mean you really don't recognise the significance of these clothes I'm wearing?
Well, they're certainly decorative...what about them?
Well, these are the furs from a larupia. Caught the creature myself I did, and these make me blend in better, see?
If you want to be successful as a hunter you've got to be as stealthy as a kyatt, as quiet as a mouse and blend in like a, well, like a larupia, I guess!

I don't know, is it?
Oh absolutely; there's a huge variety of creatures to catch around here. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds and even kyatts! Surely one of those piques your interest?
Where would I find polar kebbits?
Funnily enough, you've just put your finger right on the problem. With polar kebbits, finding them is the hardest part! You'll have to track them down.
How would I go about doing that, then?

The easiest way to get started is by looking somewhere you can be sure a kebbit will have been and then working from there. You see the holes around here leading down into the ice? They're kebbit burrows!
You'll be hard pressed to catch a polar kebbit in its home, but if you search around the entrance to a burrow then you might be able to find a trail.

Now, kebbit trails are usually fairly easy to follow once you've found them, but if the trail does peter out, you should try inspecting the surrounding scenery for clues as to where the creature may have gone.
Good places to look for clues include hollow logs in which the kebbit may have hidden or vegetation which may have been chewed or damaged.
There are also tunnels running through the ice here that the kebbits use, so you should check those out as well.
What's more, these tunnels can often help to shelter a trail from further snow, making it even easier for you to pick them up again.
Eventually, of course, the kebbit will have probably hidden somewhere. Polar kebbits don't hang about in the open for long for fear of their natural predators.
If you suspect a kebbit is close by, try looking around for signs of disturbed snow. Polar kebbits will often bury themselves in snow drifts as a means of hiding.
If you think you've found a kebbit, use a noose wand to haul the creature out from the snow.
Wow, that's quite a lot to remember.
Don't worry; if you find yourself struggling to follow a trail, just come and ask me and I'll see if I can help.
But remember, the best place to start is by searching around their burrows.
Great, thanks.
How do you hunt birds?
Ah, you can get cunning little bird snares for just that. You should be able to find them in specialist Hunter shops. Try to lay them in fairly open areas with lots of birds.
Do I need to place any bait on these traps?

No, that's not necessary. The idea is that the bird will see the trap as somewhere to perch. If the bird lands on the trigger stick, it should drop away and a small loop of wire should close around the bird's feet.
And remember, it's important to collect any captures from your traps fairly quickly; otherwise, you risk losing them to various wild scavengers.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Ah, the key there is concealment, both of yourself and your traps.
The most obvious point is to stay out of sight of your own traps. If possible, hide around a wall, hedge or similar. Failing that, make sure you're a good few feet away from your trap.
You can hide yourself even better by wearing clothing appropriate to the area in which you are hunting.
Your best bet is to use the skins of creatures native to the area. There is a very good tailor in east Varrock who may be able to help you with making clothing out of such skins.
Finally, a lot of creatures may avoid your traps if they can smell a human scent on them. This is where smoking a trap can be useful.
It takes a bit of practice, but by using the smoke from a torch, you can mask any other scents that may surround a trap.
Wow, thanks for your help.
You're welcome, good luck with the hunting.
What's so special about butterflies?
That depends entirely on the butterfly.
I'll admit that the activities of many butterflies may be of no interest at all. However, we are lucky in having around here some fine examples of rare thaumic butterflies.
These butterflies reputedly have magical powers that, when released, can make a person stronger or heal otherwise critical wounds.
At this point, I should offer a note of caution, however: it is also said that these powers will not manifest themselves if the butterflies are captured for selfish purposes.
Rather, they are gifts that must be used by one person to aid another. Of course, you'll have to catch them first.
Why, with a butterfly net of course! You should also carry some empty butterfly jars with you in which to keep the butterflies.
How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?
Ah, now for these creatures I would recommend using a deadfall trap. Deadfalls are quite easy to set up, and yet you can catch some very reasonably sized creatures with them.
Deadfall traps basically work by having a large dead weight, such as a boulder, positioned so as to be delicately balanced above some form of bait.
You will need to make sure you have a knife and some wood with you to create appropriate supports and a trigger for this sort trap.
In the case of sabre-toothed kebbits you should use some form of raw meat to bait your trap, but other animals may prefer other baits, such as fish or vegetables.
Oooh, kyatts soundsinteresting. I want to catch one of those.
Well, you've set your sights high, kyatts are incredibly fearsome creatures, but with determination like that I'm sure you'll make it.
Now, you're not going to be able to catch a kyatt with just a small box or a noose on a stick. You need a much bigger trap.
Pit traps are a good bet. You'd be best off finding a natural dip in the ground as the basis for your trap. If you dig a pit yourself, you risk creatures noticing the disturbed ground nearby.
Once you've found an appropriate spot, you'll need some logs and a knife. The logs serve two purposes.
Some can be carved into sharp skewers for the bottom of the pit; hopefully the kyatt will die when it falls onto these. Others can be used to conceal the trap.
Of course, even then the pit is going to look suspicious, so you're going to need to lure the kyatt onto the branches in some way. What actually tends to work best for this is, well, yourself!
What? I don't like the sound of that.
Yes, that's the normal response, but I kid you not. If you really want a kyatt to follow you over that pit then just give it a good poke!
Of course, I suggest you use something long to poke it with. Poking a kyatt with your finger is likely to end in unfortunate limb loss.
Fortunately, you can get very good sticks for poking from most Hunter shops.

Once you have...got the creature's attention, try to lead it to one of your traps. Make sure to jump the branches when you reach the trap yourself, of course; it would be embarrassing to fall into your own trap.
Then, if the kyatt is giving you all of its attention, hopefully it won't notice the trap, and with any luck, it will stumble right into the pit.
That sounds a bit hit or miss, and kind of suicidal too!
Well that's what makes it exciting, isn't it? But honestly, if you want to capture a kyatt, that's your best bet.
Can you teach me how to hunt?
Why certainly. I reached the peak of my abilities some time ago, but I'm more than happy to help newcomers to the field. Was there anything in particular you had in mind?
Where's the best place to start?
I always say a good starting point is to learn how to follow the creatures you want to capture. Around here, that means practicing on polar kebbits.
So how do I track them down, then?

Well, there's pretty much anything you could want to hunt. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds and even kyatts! Surely one of those interests you?

At the end of the League, you will be given a League Rank. This is based upon the number of League Points you have earned compared to the other participants.
Anyone who earns at least 100 League Points will be eligible for the Bronze rank. The top 80% of participants get the Iron rank. The top 60% get Steel.
The top 40% get Mithril. The top 20% get Adamant. The top 5% get Rune. The best participants, those who make it to the top 1%, get the Dragon rank!

First I must warn you to take every precaution to keep your RuneScape password and PIN secure. The most important thing to remember is to never give your password to, or share your account with, anyone.

I'd like to know about password security.

Well, the first thing to remember with password security, which I can't stress enough, is to never tell your password, bank PIN or authenticator details to anyone, not even if they claim to be Jagex staff. Real

Jagex staff will NEVER ask for your password. Sharing your account is a very bad idea, even if you think that you know and trust the person you are sharing with. Players have lost items and even their
account this way. Sharing accounts is also against the rules.
Is there anything else to be aware of?

Yes, also be careful where you enter your password. Be aware that fake Old School RuneScape websites exist. These are sites that claim to give things such as item/stat upgrades, free items, beta testing and
moderator applications. Jagex do not offer any of these services.

Also be aware of trojans and keyloggers. These nasty programs can send everything you type into your device back to the computers of malicious people, so you can lose more than just your Old School RuneScape

password in this way. To avoid getting these on your device, be very wary of what you download, especially when it comes to downloading third party software. Also be very wary of email attachments and instant
messenger file transfers, which can contain such things.
Finally, remember the game doesn't censor your password or bank PIN when you type them; anyone who tells you otherwise is probably trying to steal your character or items.
I'd like to know more about avoiding item scamming.

There are many nice and helpful players in Old School RuneScape; unfortunately, as in real life, there are some who aren't so honest. Some people may try to trick you out of your items. Try not to fall for this as

Jagex policy is to never return lost items to players that have been scammed. Doing so just encourages users to claim they lost items they never had to gain an unfair advantage. However, people carrying out such
scams will get banned as it is against the rules.

When trading, you have a second trade confirmation screen. Always double check that you are getting the items you expect on this page as some people may try and change what they are trading at the last minute on
the first trade screen. Remember when you have clicked accept on the second trade screen, the trade is not reversible.

Try and find out from someone else what an item is before spending a lot of money on it. Not all merchants are honest about the rarity or the uses of their wares. For example, some people try to pass off spinach rolls as
rare when in fact they're as common as cabbages!

Be wary of people offering to improve your items. For example, some people will claim they can add a trim to your armour or upgrade your sword to a more powerful one. This is not possible and they are trying
to steal your hard-earned equipment.
I'd like to know more about in-game moderation.

You will, from time to time, see moderator characters in game. Remember: a real staff member will never ask for your password or any other personal information. There are two types of moderator. You may see Jagex

staff characters in game - these can be identified by a gold crown next to their name and are the people who work in the Jagex offices. They might be from Customer Support, or they might be a tester or a

programmer. You may also see player moderators - these can be identified by a silver crown next to their name. Player moderators are trusted players of Old School RuneScape that help keep in-game behaviour in
line with the Old School RuneScape rules.
How do I become a player moderator?

The only way to become a player moderator is to know and play by the rules laid down by Jagex. Report those who break the rules, help players who need it and one day you might find an invite to become a moderator in
your Old School RuneScape inbox. Note that Jagex will never contact you in game or by email to become a player moderator.

Being a Pharaoh offers many luxuries, both in life and in death. Many strive only for these luxuries. They forget that being a Pharaoh also comes with responsibility.
My father had a responsibility greater than most. At the time of his rule, our people were locked in a great war. To hold back the Ruinous Powers, our gods granted us immensely powerful weapons.

What are these weapons?

Souls?

The weapons in my father's tomb can be used to drain a being of divine energy and transfer that energy to another. If used correctly, they would grant the Devourer true godhood.
Then I need to get into that tomb and stop her.

Now for the defensive style, this style will give you experience points in your Defensive skill. When using this style you will notice that you get hit less often.
Finally, we have the controlled style. This style will give you the same amount of experience as the other styles would but shared across all three of the combat skills.
If you were using the training sword for example, there are four different attack types. Stab, lunge, slash and block.
Each type uses one of the attack styles. Stab uses accurate, lunge and slash use aggressive and block uses defensive.

Draughts?

Runelink?

Runesquares?
Yes, you take it in turns to add a line with the goal of making squares. Everytime you make a square you take another turn.
Runeversi?

The natural historian poses as a leech...

What happens when I die in Deadman mode?
If you die to a player you will lose the 10 most valuable stacks of items from your bank, all items that you have on your person and half of the experience you have gained in any unprotected skills.

If you die to a monster when you have a PK skull you will lose the 10 most valuable stacks of items from your bank, all items that you have on your person and half of the experience you have gained in any unprotected skills.
If you die to a monster when you do not have a PK skull you will lose all of the items on your person except for the 3 most valuable. You will not lose experience or any items from your bank.
What happens when I kill a player in Deadman mode?

When you kill a player you will receive any items they have on their person and you will also be given a key. You can use this key on Deadman chests found in various banks across the map. Within the chest you will
find the 10 most valuable stacks of items from the bank of the player you struck down. From here you will be able to choose the items you would like to keep.
How can I protect my items in Deadman mode?

You can protect up to 10 items by placing them in your safe deposit box. Items in your safe deposit box will not be lost to a player who kills you, unlike those found in your bank. Remember that you can only place 10 single items into your safe deposit box, no stacks.

You can protect your levels in up to 2 combat skills and 3 non-combat skills. You can choose which by opening your items lost on death interface found in your equipment tab. Choose wisely!

Safe zones are areas patrolled by very high level guards which can be found in various places across the map. How do I play board games?

You can challenge someone to a game anywhere in the games rooms by using the right click option. Choose the type of game and then choose the options you want such as time per move. If you want to play a particular

game there are challenge rooms dedicated to that game. In the challenge rooms you can see other players ranks by right clicking them, their skill will be displayed instead of their combat level. Once you have enough

experience you will be able to use the challenge rooms on the first floor! If your opponent accepts the challenge you will be taken to one of the tables in the main room where you will play your game of choice.
Once you have finished your game you will go back to the challenge room where you can challenge again!
What games can I play?
Currently we offer Draughts, Runelink, Runesquares, and Runeversi.
Draughts?
Draughts uses standard rules, apart from: a draw is declared if no piece has been taken or promoted for forty moves. To play Draughts go to the challenge room in the SW corner.
Runelink?
Yup, you have to get four runes in row. The challenge room for Runelink is in the SE corner.
Runesquares?
Yes, you take it in turns to add a line with the goal of making squares. Everytime you make a square you take another turn. The challenge room for Runesquares is in the SW corner.
Runeversi?
Yep, the aim is to have more of your runes on the board than your opponent. You can take your opponents pieces by trapping them between your own. The challenge room for Runeversi is in the SE corner.

Draughts?

Runesquares?

Runeversi?
Yep, the aim is to have more of your runes on the board than your opponent. You can take your opponents pieces by trapping them between your own. The challenge room for Runeversi is in the SE corner.

Sorrow in what humanity did to this world, in the horrors they unleashed, in their cataclysm of despair, in the tens of thousands of species that will never walk or swim or fly again.

What is a Player Moderator?

Player Moderators are normal players of the game, just like you. However, since they have shown themselves to be trustworthy and active reporters, they have been invited by Jagex to monitor the game and

take appropriate action when they see rule breaking. You can spot a Player Moderator in game by looking at the chat screen - when a Player Moderator speaks, a silver crown appears to the left of their name.
Remember, if there's not silver crown there, they are not a Player Moderator!

What can Player Moderators do?

Player Moderators, or 'P-mods', have the ability to mute rule breakers and Jagex view their reports as a priority so that action is taken as quickly as possible. P- Mods also have access to the Player Moderator Centre.
Within the Centre are tools to help them Moderate Old School RuneScape. These tools include dedicated forums, the Player Moderator Guidelines and the Player Moderator Code of Conduct.
How do I become a Player Moderator?
Jagex picks players who spend their time and effort to help better the Old School RuneScape community. To increase your chances of becoming a Player Moderator:
Keep your account secure! This is very important, as a player with poor security will never be a P-Mod. Read our Security Tips for more information.
Play by the rules! The rules of Old School RuneScape are enforced for a reason, to make the game a fair and enjoyable environment for all.
Report accurately! When Jagex consider an account for review they look for quality, not quantity. Ensure your reports are of a high quality by following the report guidelines.
Be excellent to each other! Treat others as you would want to be treated yourself. Respect your fellow player.
What can Player Moderators not do?

P-Mods cannot ban your account - they can only report offences. Jagex then take action based on the evidence received. If you lose your password or get scammed by another player, P-Mods cannot help you

get your account back. All they can do is recommend you to go to Customer Support. They cannot retrieve any items you may have lost and receive no free items from Jagex for helping moderate the game. They are

players who give their efforts to help the community out of the goodness of their hearts! P-mods do not work for Jagex and so cannot make you a Moderator, or recommend other accounts to become moderators. If

Whatever you say.
I need more carrots..
Why? What happened?
Let's call it a quality control incident.
You drank the juice didn't you?
Perhaps.
Right well you best go see Weasel again, but he won't be happy.
Is he ever happy?
Hah! Good point! Best hurry along now!
Bye.
Ooh look at those carrots, fantastic! This juice is sure to be a treat.
Let's hope so.
You'll need a special glass for the juice, come back when you have space for one.
Here's a carrot juice glass, make sure you use this!
Isn't this just a beer glass?
Ha! Just a beer glass! You're a real joker!
It's VERY important that you use the correct glassware.
Alright, I will. Goodness me.
The juice press is in the storage room behind the bar. Have fun, and don't make too much mess!
Will do, thanks!
How's the juicing going?
Erm, I lost the glass.
Lost or broke? I'm not stupid. Those glasses are expensive you know!
Sorry, can I have another glass please?
Make some room for a new one and you can, yes.
Yes you can, but take care of it this time!
Thanks, and I will.
I'm about to get juicing!
Well hurry up, we don't want to keep the Easter Bunny waiting!
Remember, the juice press is in the storage area behind the bar.
I remember!
Then why are you still here?

Ohhhh! Look at that juice! Such colour. It smells divine too.

Well let's see what the Easter Bunny thinks.

Hello again!

That's great!

Any time.
I'm making some Easter Buns for the Easter Bunny, and I need some Easter Spices.
Do you have any I could use?

Of course I can't give you the spices unless you can carry them. Come back when you have space!
There you go, I hope they work well!
Thanks!
I bet those spices will bring those buns to life!
Judging by the smell, I'd say so. Powerful stuff.
Thanks for both juice and spices, EB really liked the buns!
Talk about carrot juice.
Talk about Easter Buns.
Hi!
Hi!

Oh...er...nothing!
Hello there, are you interested in buying one of my special capes?
What's so special about your capes?

Ahh well they make it less likely that you'll accidently attack anyone wearing the same cape as you and easier to attack everyone else. They also make it easier to distinguish people who're wearing the same cape as you
from everyone else. They're very useful when out in the wilderness with friends or anyone else you don't want to harm.
So would you like to buy one?
No thanks.
What's so special about your capes?
Yes please!
No thanks.
Hello there. What are you doing all the way out here?
Nothing you need to worry about.
So this is where you scampered off to after the monster awoke?
Look [player name], it was a simple misunderstanding, that's all...

Things got a little heated down there, but we all made it out alive, right?
Barely... I had to defeat that monster on my own!
What are you doing out here, anyway?
We thought you'd rat us out to the authorities, so we came out here to hide.
Plus, we heard there are some sealed tombs in the desert that haven't been touched in hundreds of years...
Ah, of course... scoping out your next grave to rob.
Hello youngster!
[I/We] don't talk to strange old people.
Hey who you calling old?! And strange?!
Hello again.
You think you're tough do you?
Pardon?
I can beat anyone up!
He can you know!
Really?
The boy begins to jump around with his fists up. You decide it's best not to kill him just yet.
Hello there, I've been looking for you.
I didn't mean to take it! I just forgot to pay.
What? I'm trying to help your mum find Fluffs.
Ohh...well, in that case I might be able to help. Fluffs followed me to my secret play area, I haven't seen her since.
Where is this play area?
If I told you that, it wouldn't be a secret.
Tell me sonny, or I will hurt you.
W..wh..what?! Y..you wouldn't! A young lad like me! I'd have you behind bars before nightfall!
You decided it's best not to hurt the boy.
What will make you tell me?
Well...now you ask, I am a bit short on cash.
How much?
10 coins.
10 coins?!
I'll handle this.
100 coins should cover it.
100 coins! Why should I pay you?
You shouldn't, but we won't help otherwise. We never liked that cat anyway, so what do you say?
I'm not paying you a penny.
Okay then, I'll find another way to make money.
Okay then, I'll pay.
You give the lad 100 coins.
There you go, now where did you see Fluffs ?
I play at an abandoned lumber mill to the north east. Just beyond the Jolly Boar Inn. I saw Fluffs running around in there.
Anything else?
Well, you'll have to find the broken fence to get in. I'm sure you can manage that.
Well, never mind, it's Fluffs' loss.
I'm sure my mum will get over it.
Where did you say you saw Fluffs?
Weren't you listening? I saw the flea bag in the old lumber mill just north east of here. Just walk past the Jolly Boar Inn and you should find it.
My brother reckons I can't solve this puzzle. I can't have him laughing at me! Do me a favour and solve it for me.
Sorry but you haven't solved the puzzle yet.
Thanks [mister/miss]!
Tell me sonny, or I will hurt you.
What will make you tell me?
I'm not paying you a penny.
Okay then, I'll pay.
Well never mind, it's Fluffs' loss.
I've got you the limpwurt roots!
Good! Good! My potion is nearly ready! Bubble, bubble, toil and trouble!
Now we shows them ours magic! Hold on tight!
A cutscene is shown where the player is teleported across the lava.
Hehe! We see you're in a pickle!
Wants to be getting over the nasty lava do we?
Nah, not bothered!
Hehe! Ye'll come back! They always come back!
Mocking us are we? Clever one aren't we?
I'm knowing some magic trickesses! I could get over easy as that!
Don't tell them! They always come! They pester poor Winelda!
If you're such a great witch, get me over!
See! They pester Winelda!
I can do something for you!
Good! Don't pester! Help!
Get Winelda 20 limpwurt roots for my pot.
Then we shows them some magic!
Yes I do!
Have you got roots for poor Winelda?
How many did you need again?
We needs 20 Limpwurt roots for pot.
I've got some limpwurt roots!
We needs 20 rooteses!
Hi again. Could you do the honours again please?
Certainly! We helps those that helps poor Winelda!
Nah, not bothered!
Yes we do!
Yes I do!
It's a bit hot and dry round here for a gnome isn't it? I thought you gnomes liked your home comforts.
Certainly I miss home cooking, but gnomes are also fundamentally curious people. I'm here exploring the furthest reaches of the world for the King.
Found anything interesting?

Sophanem is a curious place, if you can get into the blighted place. There are several pyramids round here as well. Fascinating architecture, I've heard stories that some of them contain treasure tombs and mummies.
Cats seem to have considerable importance round here, they certainly seem tied into their religion. The Gods round here seem very alien to me - I've never heard of them before.
Thanks.
What does this mint cake do?
Gnomish mint cake is a great source of energy for the gnome traveller. It will give you that extra bit of zip when you are running out of steam.
Ooh, that might come in very handy. Do you have any spare?
I need all the mint cake I have, I'm afraid.
What does this seed pod do?

Ah, the seed pod of the Grand Tree is a fascinating spirit artefact. It is a very useful thing, though one must treat it with respect, since the Grand Tree has a connection with all of its parts, however distant they
may be. How do you think the Spirit Trees work?

If you launch its seeds in a far flung location, you will be helping the tree survive, so the grand tree will help a gnome glider pilot find you, using the seed burst itself (which marks the sky) and a little magic, and bring you
back home as an act of gratitude. Budding farmers will also find their link with plants to be just a little bit better than before.
However, it takes time for a pilot to find you, and if you are in a real hurry, and I mean a real emergency, you can just squash the seed pod. The Grand Tree doesn't like this, but will pull you back

home straight away. Don't do this if you need to do anything with plants straight away, though - your fingers will be considerably less green for a while after using the seed pod this way, and the journey is not
very pleasant...
Wow, that's very interesting. Thanks.
Here, solve this.
Wingstone hands you a [light box/puzzlebox]!
That doesn't look solved to me.
Well done [player name]. Here you go.
You've obtained a [new clue/casket]!
You hand over your delivery of [a/some] [ordered gnome food item] to Wingstone.
This will hit the spot. Oh yes. Thanks.
Now that I have some proper food, I won't need this any more.
Here, take these Grand Seed pods. Very useful in emergencies!
I was given this odd device, maybe you can do something with it.
You must have had to travel a long way to get this to me. Here's a little something extra as a tip.
You are given [a/some] [reward item(s)] as a tip.
It's a bit hot and dry round here for a gnome isn't it?
What does this mint cake do?
What does this seed pod do?
Why are you in that cage?
That evil witch put me in here! She kidnapped me!
That's awful! Why did she do that?
She wanted the secret of my ogleroots, so she did!
Your ogleroots? I don't think I understand. What secret is that?
Well now, I have perfected a spell that would grow an ogleroot to an enormous size.
That's amazing! But how do you move the ogleroot around if it's so big?

You know, I had the very same problem so I came up with a simple solution. I used a spell I learned from a chap called Larry to shrink 'em down really small so that I could carry whole bags filled with 'em to the market place. Then when I got there, I would use the growing spell once more to make 'em huge and sell 'em for a tidy sum.
That's amazing! So how does the witch fit in to all this?

Well that old witch - she's a sly one, I tell you. She found out about my spell and kidnapped me along with my bag of ogleroots. She wants the secret of the spell but I ain't talking! No sir! So she's been feeding my mini-ogleroots to those ugly...things over there.
So she hasn't found out the spell yet?
Not yet, no. And I still ain't telling her. But from what I gather, she's started to use them ogleroots in some of her potions for something. I don't know what, though.
I see. Can I get you out of there somehow?
No, it's ok. I want to keep an eye on what the witch is up to down here with these odd creatures.
So, will you be alright?
Yes, I'll be fine for now. Good luck with your tasks!
This could be worse I guess. Oh wait... No it can't.
I'm hungry...
Sometimes I wish this thing would just escape. At least we'd have something to do then.
It's so cold...
Greetings, [player name].
So you're a wise old man, huh?
Less of the 'old' man, if you please!
But yes, I suppose you could say that. I prefer to think of myself as a sage.
So what's a sage doing here?

I've spent most of my life studying this world in which we live. I've strode through the depths of the deadliest dungeons, roamed the murky jungles of Karamja, meditated on the glories of Saradomin on Entrana,
and read some dusty tomes in the Library of Varrock.
Now I'm not as young as I used to be, I'm settling here where it's peaceful.
It's a pity about that vampyre that keeps attacking the village. At least Saradomin protects me.
That's quite an exciting life you've had.
Exciting? Yes, I suppose so.
Now I'm here, perhaps I could offer you the benefit of my experience and wisdom?
Thanks! So you can help me?
Well, I imagine you've gathered up quite a lot of stuff on your travels. Things you used for quests a long time ago that you don't need now.
If you like, I can look through your bank and see if there's anything you can chuck away.
Alternatively, you can bring items here and show them to me. If I see that it's something you don't need, I'll let you know. I might even be willing to buy it.
So you'll help me clear junk out of my bank?
Yes, that's right. Or I'd be happy to chat with you about the wonders of this world!
Could I have some free stuff, please?
Deary deary me...
I'm not giving out free money, but if you try again later I'd be glad to reward you if you'd do a little job for me.
I'm not giving out free money, but I'd be happy to reward you if you'll do a little job for me.
Ok, what do you want me to do?
I'm sure I can think of a few little jobs. This won't be a quest, mind you, just a little favour...
Thanks, maybe some other time.
I'd just like to ask you something.
Please do!
Is there anything I can do for you?
Could you check my items for junk, please?
Can I get another hood for my Quest Point Cape?
You don't appear to have enough space in your inventory. Come back and see me when you do.
Can I buy a Quest Point Cape, please?
Gladly, though they cost 99,000 coins.
Okay, 99,000 coins is fine.
All skillcapes come with a hood - you're not going to be able to hold them now. Try again another time.
I'll have to come back another time.
Actually, no thanks.
Is there anything I can do for you?
Thanks, but I don't have anything I need doing right now.
Could you tell me about the Wilderness, please?
If Entrana is a land dedicated to the glory of Saradomin, the Wilderness is surely the land of Zamorak.
It's a dangerous place, where adventurers such as yourself may attack each other, using all their combat skills in the struggle for survival.
The Wilderness has different levels. In a low level area, you can only fight adventurers whose combat level is close to yours.
But if you venture into the high level areas in the far north, you can be attacked by adventurers who are significantly stronger than you.
Of course, you'd be able to attack considerably weaker people too, so it can be worth the risk.
If you dare to go to the far north-west of the Wilderness, there's a building called the Mage Arena where you can learn to summon the power of Saradomin himself!
Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
Yes please.
As you wish. Farewell, [player name].
What can you tell me about jungles?
If it's jungle you want, look no further than the southern regions of Karamja.
Once you get south of Brimhaven, the whole island is pretty much covered in exotic trees, creepers and shrubs.
There's a small settlement called Tai Bwo Wannai Village in the middle of the island. It's a funny place; the chieftain's an unfriendly chap and his sons are barking mad.
Honestly, one of them asked me to stuff a dead monkey with seaweed so he could EAT it!
Yes, I've met them.
Further south you'll find Shilo Village. It's been under attack by terrifying zombies in recent months, if my sources are correct.
I've dealt with them, although there are a few still knocking about.
The jungle's filled with nasty creatures. There are vicious spiders that you can hardly see before they try to bite your legs off, and great big jungle ogres.
Tell me about what's underground.
Oh, the dwarven realms?
Yes, there was a time, back in the Fourth Age, when we humans wouldn't have been able to venture underground. That was before we had magic; the dwarves were quite a threat.
Still, it's much more friendly now. You can visit the vast dwarven mine if you like; the entrance is on the mountain north of Falador.
If you go further west you may be able to visit the dwarven city of Keldagrim. But they were a bit cautious about letting humans in, last time I asked.

On the other hand, if you go west of Brimhaven, you'll find a huge underground labyrinth full of giants, demons, dogs and dragons to fight. It's even bigger than the caves under Taverley, although the Taverley
dungeon's pretty good for training your combat skills.
What mystical realms can I visit?
Well, you've been to Zanaris. I met a fairy years ago who said she lived there. She was an incredible warrior, considering that she wasn't even a metre tall.
Also, in my research I came across ancient references to some kind of Abyss. Demons from the Abyss have already escaped into this land; Saradomin be thanked that they are very rare!
I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.
Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.
Yeah, there isn't much left there.
What's the biggest monster in the world?
There's a mighty fire-breathing dragon living underground in the deep Wilderness, known as the King Black Dragon. It's a fearsome beast, with a breath that can poison you, freeze you to the ground or
incinerate you where you stand.
But even more deadly is the Queen of the Kalphites. As if her giant mandibles of death were not enough, she also throws her spines at her foes with deadly force. She can even cast rudimentary spells.
Some dark power must be protecting her, for she can block attacks using prayer just as humans do.
Another beast that's worthy of a special mention is the Shaikahan. It dwells in the eastern reaches of Karamja, and is almost impossible to kill except with specially prepared weapons.
Actually, that one's dead. I've been helping a barmy hunter who'd sworn to kill it.
What does poison do?
Many monsters use poison against their foes. If you get poisoned, you will not feel it at the time, but later you will begin to suffer its effects, and your life will drain slowly from you.
Over time the effects dwindle to nothing, but if you had already been wounded you might die before they wear off completely.
Fortunately, followers of Guthix have devised potions that can cure the poison or even give immunity to it.
Should you wish to use poison against your own enemies and those of our Lord Saradomin, there is a potion that you can smear on your daggers, arrows, spears, javelins and throwing knives.
What monsters drop good items?
As a general rule, tougher monsters drop more valuable items. But even a lowly hobgoblin can drop valuable gems; it just does this extremely rarely.
If you can persuade the Slayer Masters to train you as a Slayer, you will be able to fight certain monsters that drop valuable items far more often.
You might care to invest in an enchanted dragonstone ring. These are said to make a monster drop its most valuable items a little more often.
What are these strange monsters that keep appearing out of nowhere and attacking me when I'm training?
Ah, I imagine you see a lot of those.

Creatures such as the rock golem, river troll and tree spirit dwell in places where adventurers frequently go to train their skills. While you're training you will often disturb one by accident. It will then get angry and
attack you. The safest way to deal with them is to run away immediately, but they sometimes drop valuable items if you kill them.
Tell me about valiant heroes!
Ha ha ha... There are plenty of heroes. Always have been, always will be, until the fall of the world.
If you'd do a few more quests, you'd soon become a fairly noted adventurer yourself.
You're quite a noted adventurer yourself!
But I suppose I could tell you of a couple...

Yes, there was a man called Arrav. No-one knew where he came from, but he was a fearsome fighter, a skillful hunter and a remarkable farmer. He lived in the ancient settlement of Avarrocka, defending it from
goblins, until he went forth in search of some strange artefact long desired by the dreaded Mahjarrat.
Perhaps some day I shall be able to tell you what became of him.

But do not let your head be turned by heroics. Randas was another great man, but he let himself be beguiled into turning to serve Zamorak, and they say he is now a mindless creature deep in the Underground Pass that
leads to Isafdar.
Where did humans learn to use magic?
Ah, that was quite a discovery! It revolutionised our way of life and jolted us into this Fifth Age of the world.

They say a traveller in the north discovered the key, although no records state exactly what he found. From this he was able to summon the magic of the four elements, using magic as a tool and a weapon. He and
his followers learnt how to bind the power into little stones so that others could use it.
in the land south of here they constructed an immense tower where the power could be studied, but followers of Zamorak destroyed it with fire many years ago, and most of the knowledge was lost.
Perhaps one day those lost secrets will be uncovered once more.
I hear you've been very helpful to the wizards who are working on the mysteries of the rune stones.
Well, I didn't do much...
I suppose you'd know about the history of today's cities?
Yes, there are fairly good records of the formation of the cities from primitive settlements.
In the early part of the Fourth Age, of course, there were no permanent settlements. Tribes wandered the lands, staying where they could until the resources were exhausted.

This changed as people learnt to grow crops and breed animals, and now there are very few of the old nomadic tribes. There's at least one tribe roaming between the Troll Stronghold and Rellekka, though.
Yes, I've met them. They're all mad.
Truly, their faith in natural spirits is rather foolish, but they're a pleasant enough people.
Anyway, what was I saying? Ah, yes...
One settlement was Avarrocka, a popular trading centre.
In the west, Ardougne gradually formed under the leadership of the Carnillean family, despite the threat of the Mahjarrat warlord Hazeel who dwelt in that area until his downfall.
He'll be back, just you wait!
Oh dear, I hope you haven't done anything rash!
I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.
So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.
Tell me about yourself, old man.
Ah, so you want to know about me, eh?
Mmm... what could I say about myself? Let's see what I've done...
I've delved into the dungeon west of Brimhaven and heard the terrifying CRASH of the steel dragons battling each other for territory.
I spent some years on Entrana, where I learnt the techniques of pure meditation.
I've wandered through the vast desert that lies south of Al Kharid and seen the great walls of Menaphos and Sophanem.
That feline statue you've got on your bookshelf there - I'm sure I saw something like that when I was in Sophanem.
I've always liked to collect little trinkets to remind me of the time when my life was more - ah - exciting.
So you've spoken to the Sphinx, then?
Spoken to a sphinx, you say? My dear young lady, you can't possibly be serious!
What do you mean?
Ha ha ha! The people who live deep in the shifting sands of the desert will often tell travellers tall tales of strange beasts, but that doesn't mean any of it's remotely true!
But I've met the Sph...
Please, adventurer, there is nothing to be gained by interfering in matters you do not understand.
Even if such a creature were to exist...
... which it does...
EVEN IF SUCH A CREATURE WERE TO EXIST it would be terribly dangerous for you to get involved in its business.
I have heard of terrible things happening to travellers in that land, and I would not wish for you to be dragged into anything like that.
Indeed, I have heard of adventurers doing the most shameful and blasphemous deeds believing themselves to be acting on behalf of some false god!
Hmmm?
So please do not speak to me of this matter again. Now, I believe I was telling you of my adventurous youth...
Apart from all that, I've spent many a happy hour in dusty libraries, searching through ancient scrolls and texts for the wisdom of those who have passed on.
Plus plenty of other adventures, quests, journeys... Is there anything else you'd like to know?
I heard that Gielinor has three gods.
Indeed. This is correct: Saradomin, Guthix and Zamorak.
Saradomin, the great and glorious, gives life to this world.
Zamorak craves only death and destruction.
Guthix, calling itself a god of 'balance', holds no allegiance, but simply aids whatever cause suits its shifting purpose.
So who's Zaros?
What did you say?
I discovered a buried altar to a god called Zaros.
Please, do not speak further of this. No good can come of meddling in such things.
So Zaros is real?
Adventurer, my patience is limited. Speak to me no further of this - this - this foolishness.
Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?
ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!
I've heard of another god, called Armadyl.
What is this of which you speak?
A strange man asked me to go into the Temple of Ikov and steal the Staff of Armadyl.
And what makes you believe in this 'Armadyl'?
Well, there were servants of Armadyl living down in the depths of the temple. They'd been there for generations, guarding the staff.
So you trusted the word of these people who had been sitting down a hole all their lives?
Um... Yes, I suppose so.
I wouldn't worry about this sacred 'armadyllo' anymore. Just another foolish myth.
Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.
That is an impressive feat, adventurer. Truly you must be beloved in the eyes of Saradomin.
It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.
YOU'VE DONE WHAT?
Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.
How about Tumeken, Elindis, Icthlarin and the Devourer?
What names are these?
Down in Sophanem, they've got a chief god named Tumeken, plus a fertility goddess named Elindis. Icthlarin is their god of the dead and the Devourer...
Adventurer, what folly leads you to think any of these - things, exist?
But I've met Icthlarin! He'dgot a jackal's head!
It is hot in that land, and the heat can affect a traveller in strange ways. Tell me, when you met 'Icthlarin', had you been feeling at all unwell?
Well, now you mention it, I'd just been hypnotised by a weird woman I met in the desert.
So a strange woman interfered with your mind, then you met a man with the head of a jackal, and you decided he must be a god?
Umm...
Well, make sure you don't get hypnotised again, and I'm sure you'll not meet any more jackal-headed men claiming to be gods!
But...?
It'd probably be best if you don't go there again.
But you've been all around that area, haven't you? When you were travelling?
Indeed, I have.
So you'd know all about their gods?
I know what I know.
And knowing what I know, I do not speak of this matter. Perhaps you would be wise to heed my example.
I wanna know about the wars of the gods!
Ah, that was a terrible time. The armies of Saradomin fought gloriously against the minions of Zamorak, but many brave warriors and noble cities were overthrown and destroyed utterly.
You have visited Uzer, and seen for yourself the damage that could be wrought by an elder-demon in its wrath.
How did it all end?
Before the Zamorakian forces could be utterly routed, Lord Saradomin took pity on them and the battle- scarred world, and allowed a truce.
What are the Mahjarrat?
Very little is written about the tribe of the Mahjarrat. They are believed to be from the realm of Freneskae, or Frenaskrae - the spelling in this tongue is only approximate.
One of them, the foul Zamorak, has achieved godhood, although none knows how this came about.
Other Mahjarrat who have been particularly active upon this plane are Hazeel, Lucien, Azzanadra and Zemouregal.
Hazeel will rise again, you'll see!
Adventurer, your actions fill me with concern!
I've defeated Lucien.
Truly, your bravery exceeds your stature. But I fear his defeat will not be permanent.
I've met Lucien. He paid me very nicely for bringing him a staff he wanted.
Traveller, I beg of you, do not have further dealings with such creatures! You do not know their power as I do.
Azzanadra taught me some ancient magical powers after I unlocked the pyramid where he had been trapped.
Leave me, traveller; I am old, and your words fill me with horror.
Can I wield the power of Saradomin myself?
I see you are already learning to summon the power of Saradomin.

If you travel to the Mage Arena in the north-west reaches of the Wilderness, the battle mage Kolodion may be willing to let you learn to summon the power of Saradomin, should you be able to pass his test.
I want to ask you about your hat.
Why, thank you! I rather like it myself.
Did you steal it from the bank?
Me? Steal from the bank? Whatever do you mean?
There's been a break-in at Draynor Bank, and I bet you did it.
Oh my goodness, what in the world could make you think I did such a thing?
Well, you've been sitting here looking at the bank ever since you moved into this house. Now someone's robbed the bank, and suddenly your house is full of expensive stuff!
Oh dear, oh dear...
So what do you think I did? March across the street, smash the bank wall, knock out the bankers and steal all the money?
I'm an old man! I walk with a stick! How could I possibly have done that?
So you didn't rob the bank?
Just run along now, be a good lad, and don't worry yourself about me or my finances!
Hmmm... But I'll be keeping an eye on you.
Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?
You stole it off that woman in the bank! You stole all this valuable stuff too!
